PRODUCT REQUIREMENTS . INTERNAL TOOLS
Competencies
One screen where a consultant tells us what they are good at - and it sticks the moment they click.
THE PROBLEM
We cannot answer "who knows Jira?" without asking people. The competency data we do have is stale, and the app that holds it is the reason why.
Today that data lives in a Power Apps screen. Three things go wrong with it. The grid crawls once the catalogue is at full size, so people give up scrolling. The labels stopped matching how the business talks - we say competency and advanced, the screen says skill and practitioner. And the screen has a Save button, so a consultant who ticks four boxes and closes the tab saves nothing. Every one of those is a reason for someone to abandon a half-finished assessment, and a half-finished assessment is worse than none - it looks like an answer.
We are rebuilding it as a small Next.js/React app. The bet is narrow: make recording a level a single click that needs no saving, and people will keep their own profile current.
WHAT GOOD LOOKS LIKE :selected: / A consultant can open the app, find the competency they have in mind, and record their level without thinking about the mechanics - no save step, no second screen. :selected: Nothing is ever lost to a closed tab. If a click did not reach the database, the person finds out immediately rather than believing a claim was recorded. :selected: / Someone returning after two months can see only what the catalogue gained since they were last here, instead of re-reading a thousand rows. :selected: " The words on the screen match the words the business uses, so nobody has to translate practitioner into advanced in their head.
WHO THIS IS FOR
One audience, and only one: the consultant assessing themselves. Around a thousand people have accounts; expect fifty or so on the app at the same time on a busy day. They are not administrators. They come in from a desktop browser, occasionally, for a few minutes, looking for the handful of competencies that describe them inside a catalogue of roughly a thousand.
Managers, reviewers and staffing are not users of this release. Nobody validates anybody's claims and nobody browses anyone else's profile here. :unselected: :unselected: :unselected:
IN AND OUT
We are building :selected: / Browsing the competency catalogue and narrowing it down :selected: / Recording, changing and clearing your own level
/ Signing in with corporate SSO :selected:
We are not building
x Manager, reviewer or validation views - claims are :selected: self-declared and unmoderated
× Any way to edit the catalogue itself; Types, Areas :selected: and Competencies are maintained elsewhere and this app only reads them
x Cross-employee search or reporting - no "who :selected: knows X", no exports, no dashboards
THE SCREEN WE ARE REPLACING

Atlassian / Jira Align :unselected: :unselected: :unselected:
Today's Power Apps screen, marked up in red with everything that changes. Treat the picture as a sketch of intent, not a spec of pixels - the wording and the behaviour below are what we are committing to.
What stays
The shape of the thing is right and we are keeping it: one flat grid, one row per competency, showing its Type, its Area and its name, with three tick columns for the level. Above the grid, a filter row with a Type dropdown, an Area dropdown and a free-text box for the competency name. Rows come out sorted by Type, then Area, then competency name, so the grid reads the same way every time.
What changes
New words
The screen is titled Competencies, not Skills. The third column is Competency, not Skill. The middle level is Advanced, not Practitioner. Learner and Expert keep their names. This is the vocabulary we are standardising on - it should be identical everywhere the app speaks.
Toggles move up
Mine and New leave the filter row and live in the header bar, where they read as modes of the whole screen rather than one more filter among four.
Three things go
The home icon and the info icon both disappear - there is one screen, so there is nowhere to go home to and nothing to explain in a modal. The Save button and its unsaved-change counter go too. Neither should exist anywhere on the new screen.
The Save button is the point. Removing it is not a tidy-up - it is the change that fixes the stale-data problem. Everything about the writing behaviour below follows from there being nothing to click at the end. :unselected: :unselected: :unselected: :unselected: :unselected:
HOW IT BEHAVES
FINDING THE RIGHT ROWS
As a consultant, I want to drill into one family of competencies, so I am not scrolling past a thousand rows to reach the ten that describe me.
Picking a Type narrows the Area dropdown to that Type's Areas and the grid to that Type's rows. The two dropdowns are a hierarchy, so Areas from other Types never appear.
DONE WHEN
- Picking Type "Agility" leaves only that Type's Areas selectable, and only its rows in the grid.
- Changing the Type clears whatever Area was selected rather than leaving a stale pairing.
As a consultant, I want to type the name of the thing I know, because that is faster than navigating to it.
Typing in the competency box leaves only the rows whose competency name contains what was typed, ignoring case and accents.
DONE WHEN
- Typing "jira" leaves "Atlassian / Jira" and "Atlassian / Jira Align" and nothing else.
- Text that matches nothing shows a plain "No competencies match this filter" rather than an empty grid.
As a consultant, I want to review what I have already claimed, because correcting an old profile is a different job from filling a new one.
With Mine switched on, the grid shows only competencies where this person has a level recorded. Everything else drops away.
DONE WHEN
- Rated competencies stay, unrated ones disappear.
- Someone who has never rated anything sees "You have not rated any competency yet", not a blank screen.
As a consultant, I want to see only what is new since I was last here, so a two-month gap does not mean re-reading the whole catalogue.
With New switched on, the grid shows only competencies that were added to the catalogue after the last time this person changed any of their own levels. "New" is personal and relative - it is not a fixed window like "the last 30 days". Someone who last touched their levels forty-five days ago sees exactly what the catalogue gained in those forty-five days. Someone who has never recorded a level sees everything, because all of it is new to them.
DONE WHEN
- An employee whose last change was forty-five days ago sees the competencies added in that window and nothing older.
- Once they change any level, switching New back on shows nothing until the catalogue grows again.
- Clearing every level they hold does not reset their personal watermark - it survives.
RECORDING WHERE YOU ARE :unselected: :unselected: :unselected: :unselected: :unselected: :unselected: :unselected: :unselected: :unselected: :unselected:
As a consultant, I want one level per competency, because "I am a Learner and an Expert at Jira" is not a thing a person can be.
Ticking a level on a row that already holds a different one records the new level and clears the old, leaving exactly one of Learner, Advanced, Expert ticked on that row. Re-ticking the level you already hold is a no-op - it should not generate a second write.
DONE WHEN
- A row at Learner, clicked on Expert, ends with only Expert ticked and Expert stored.
- Clicking the level already held changes nothing and writes nothing.
As a consultant, I want to take a claim back, because a mis-click should not become a permanent statement about me.
Unticking the level a row currently holds deletes the claim outright and returns the row to unrated - which is a real state, distinct from "Learner".
DONE WHEN
- The row ends with nothing ticked and no stored record at all.
- With Mine on, the row leaves the view, since it is no longer one of mine.
As a consultant, I want my click to be the whole interaction, so I never lose work by closing a tab.
Every level change is written as it happens, with no further action from the person. There is no Save button, no counter, no "you have unsaved changes" prompt.
DONE WHEN
- A level picked, then the page reloaded, still shows that level.
- After several changes, no save control and no change counter appear anywhere.
As a consultant, I want to be told when a click did not land, because silence would let me believe something false was recorded about me.
If a level change fails to write, the row goes back to its last saved level and a non-blocking message names the competency and says it was not saved. The person is never left looking at a tick that does not exist in the database. A write that is merely slow, but succeeds, is left alone.
DONE WHEN
- With writes failing, the row reverts and the message names the competency that did not save.
- A slow-but-successful write is not reverted and raises no error.
GETTING IN
As a consultant, I want to just be signed in, because this is an internal tool and I already have a corporate identity.
Opening any page unauthenticated sends the person to Microsoft Entra ID and brings them back to the page they asked for, signed in as their directory identity. Whose assessments are read and written is resolved from that session - never from anything the browser sends.
DONE WHEN
- After signing in, the grid shows that person's own assessments.
- Cancelling at the Microsoft prompt lands on a sign-in page with a retry, not on the grid. :unselected: :unselected: :unselected: :unselected: :unselected: :unselected: :unselected: :unselected: :unselected: :unselected:
HOW IT FITS TOGETHER
SYSTEM CONTEXT
Consultant
rates competencies
Competencies this product Next.js / React · PostgreSQL
authenticates
person records own levels
Microsoft Entra ID external corporate identity
browser, HTTPS
OIDC
Power Apps "Skills" - retired one-time migration source
seeds the catalogue once, by export
The app stands alone. It owns its own PostgreSQL database and has exactly one live dependency - Microsoft Entra ID, for sign- in over OIDC with the authorization-code flow and PKCE. The dashed line is a one-time load of the catalogue and the existing assessments out of the old Power Apps app; after go-live there is no connection between the two.
What we store
The catalogue Type - Area - Competency
Read-only to this app - it is maintained elsewhere and loaded in. Each competency carries the date it was added to the catalogue, which is what the New toggle compares against.
The person
A directory identity, keyed on their Entra object id, created the first time they sign in. It also carries the moment they last changed any level. That timestamp is the other half of the New toggle, and it has to survive them clearing every level they hold - so it belongs on the person, not derived from their claims.
The claim
One person, one competency, one level: Learner, Advanced or Expert. At most one of these per person per competency - the storage itself should make two impossible, rather than relying on the screen to prevent it. No record at all means unrated. This is personal data: we keep it until twelve months after the person's account is disabled, and it never goes into logs.
WHAT WE ARE COUNTING ON
- The catalogue keeps being maintained outside this app. If that changes, someone has to build an editor and this document grows a section.
- Everyone who needs the app already has a corporate Entra ID account. There are no local accounts and no invitation flow.
- Before launch we need an export of the current catalogue and everyone's existing assessments out of Power Apps, from whoever owns that app. It has to carry each competency's original date of addition - if the migration stamps everything with today's date, the New toggle is wrong for every existing employee from day one.
- At the start of the build we need an Entra ID app registration per environment, with redirect URIs and credentials, from the corporate identity team.
OPEN QUESTIONS
? Telling people a write failed is our idea, not yours. Nobody asked for it, but with the Save button gone a failed write is otherwise invisible and the person walks away believing a false claim was recorded. We think it is not optional. Confirm before we build it.
? Should unrated and "I have looked at this and it does not apply to me" be the same thing? Today they are - a blank row means both. If staffing ever wants to distinguish "nobody has assessed this" from "nobody here can do this", the model needs a fourth state and we should know now rather than after migration. :unselected: :unselected: :unselected: :unselected: :unselected: :unselected: :unselected:
